entry_conditions: Migration upgrade executed: ReseedSilo.init runs reseedSiloDeposit once per whitelisted token. Any account that held deposits in 2+ tokens on L1 (e.g. Bean AND BEAN:ETH).
violation_path: ReseedSilo.init calls reseedSiloDeposit(beanDeposits)
for account A: s.accts[A].stalk = accountStalk_bean (line 164, assignment)
reseedSiloDeposit(beanEthDeposits) runs
for same account A: s.accts[A].stalk = accountStalk_beanEth (OVERWRITES, not +=)
attacker_class: no attacker needed — protocol-wide accounting bug affecting every multi-token depositor
impact_estimate: Every account with deposits in more than one token loses all stalk except that from the last-reseeded token (urBeanLp). Loss of governance weight and earned-Bean share for the majority of large depositors. Permanent on L2.
evidence: ReseedSilo.sol:164 `s.accts[deposits.accounts].stalk = accountStalk;` uses `=`. The loop structure processes one token per reseedSiloDeposit call; init() calls it 6 times for 6 tokens against the same s.accts mapping.

entry_conditions: A contract account redeems via L2ContractMigrationFacet.redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances with a valid merkle proof + signature.
violation_path: addMigratedDepositsToAccount declares uint128 totalDeposited; uint128 totalDepositedBdv (both 0)
loop adds per-deposit amounts to s.accts but NEVER increments totalDeposited/totalDepositedBdv
line 194-195: s.sys.silo.balances[token].deposited = totalDeposited (=0); .depositedBdv = totalDepositedBdv (=0)
attacker_class: unprivileged (any whitelisted migrant) — but also a latent protocol bug
impact_estimate: Global silo balances for the migrated token are overwritten to 0 while per-account deposits are credited. Breaks total-vs-sum invariant: BDV/withdraw/convert math underflows or misprices; can brick withdrawals or be leveraged for inflation. High/Critical accounting corruption.
evidence: L2ContractMigrationFacet.sol:158-160 declares totalDeposited/totalDepositedBdv, never written in loop; lines 194-195 assign them (0) to global s.sys.silo.balances[token].

entry_conditions: Attacker obtains one valid (owner, deposits, proof) leaf and the owner's EIP-712 signature over (owner, reciever, deadline) before deadline. Signature/proof are public once submitted on-chain.
violation_path: redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances(owner, reciever, ..., signature) succeeds first time
no nonce / spent[owner] / spent[leaf] marker is written
the SAME calldata is submitted again before deadline
verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances passes (same proof), verifySignature passes (same sig, deadline not expired)
addMigratedDepositsToAccount re-runs, re-setting deposits and re-adding stalk/roots to reciever
attacker_class: unprivileged — anyone can resubmit observed calldata
impact_estimate: No replay protection. setStalk uses += (lines 206-207) so each replay adds stalk and roots again, inflating governance weight and earned Bean for reciever without backing. Deposits are re-set (idempotent) but stalk/roots accumulate. Plausible Critical if reciever is attacker-controlled.
evidence: L2ContractMigrationFacet.sol: no nonce/mapping written; verifySignature only checks deadline+signer; setStalk lines 206-207 use s.accts[account].stalk += / roots +=. Replay window = until deadline.

entry_conditions: ReseedField.init invoked during migration with any account having >=1 plot.
violation_path: outer loop i over accountPlots
inner loop header: for (uint j; j < accountPlots[i].plots.length; i++) — increments i, not j
j stays 0; i increments, accountPlots[i] eventually reads out-of-bounds -> revert; or wrong account indexing before that
attacker_class: no attacker — deterministic bug that bricks Field migration
impact_estimate: ReseedField.init reverts (index OOB) for any input with plots, so the migration upgrade transaction fails / Field can never be reseeded. If somehow it does not revert it assigns wrong plots. Migration DoS — funds (pods) cannot be brought to L2.
evidence: ReseedField.sol:49 `for (uint j; j < accountPlots[i].plots.length; i++)` — the post-statement increments i instead of j.

entry_conditions: External L1 Bean holder burns Beans on L1 via BeanL2MigrationFacet.migrateL2Beans; bridge relays recieveL1Beans on L2.
violation_path: recieveL1Beans(reciever, amount) called by bridge
s.sys.migration.migratedL1Beans += amount (now > 0)
require(EXTERNAL_L1_BEANS >= s.sys.migration.migratedL1Beans) with EXTERNAL_L1_BEANS == 0
0 >= (amount>0) is false -> revert
attacker_class: no attacker — bug causes guaranteed fund loss for honest migrants
impact_estimate: EXTERNAL_L1_BEANS is hardcoded constant 0. Every external Bean migration reverts on L2 AFTER the user already burned Beans on L1 (BeanL2MigrationFacet.migrateL2Beans burns first, line 49). Permanent loss of all externally-held Beans that attempt migration. High/Critical.
evidence: BeanL1RecieverFacet.sol:22 `uint256 constant EXTERNAL_L1_BEANS = 0;` and line 39-42 require check; BeanL2MigrationFacet.sol:49 burns before sending message.

entry_conditions: Any code path that requests a manipulation-resistant TWAP price via LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice(addr, timeout, lookback>0).
violation_path: getTokenPrice(addr, maxTimeout, lookback)
return lookback > 0 ? getPrice(addr,maxTimeout) : getTwap(addr,maxTimeout,lookback)
lookback>0 (TWAP requested) -> getPrice = INSTANTANEOUS spot price (no TWAP smoothing)
lookback==0 (spot requested) -> getTwap with lookback=0 -> div by lookback (0) in final return -> revert/0
attacker_class: unprivileged if a spot-priced path feeds a financial decision; otherwise medium
impact_estimate: Inverted ternary: TWAP requests silently degrade to manipulable spot price, defeating oracle manipulation resistance for any consumer (peg/deltaB/USD pricing). Spot requests divide by zero. Severity depends on whether a reachable mint/convert path uses lookback>0 here — if so, flash-loan price manipulation. High.
evidence: LibChainlinkOracle.sol:44-47 ternary is inverted relative to the documented contract (lookback>0 should be TWAP).

entry_conditions: A frozen/broken Chainlink feed during a price query that flows through LibUsdOracle.getUsdPrice/getTokenPriceFromExternal.
violation_path: LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice returns 0 (documented failure mode)
getTokenPriceFromExternal line 120-127: return uint256(1e24).div(0) -> revert
or getUsdPrice line 53/58/64: 1e24/0 guarded by ==0 checks in getUsdPrice but NOT in the encodeType==1 branch of getTokenPriceFromExternal
attacker_class: no attacker — availability bug under feed failure
impact_estimate: Where 1e24.div(chainlinkPrice) is computed without a prior ==0 guard (encodeType 0x01 branch), a frozen feed reverts the whole call instead of returning 0, DoSing any consumer (sunrise/convert) that expected graceful degradation. Medium DoS.
evidence: LibUsdOracle.sol:120-127 divides 1e24 by LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice(...) with no zero-check, contradicting the 'returns 0 rather than reverting' contract.

entry_conditions: A token whose oracleImplementation has a custom (non-0x01/0x02) encodeType and a target contract.
violation_path: getTokenPriceFromExternal falls through to target.staticcall(selector, lookback)
if !success return 0
else assembly { tokenPrice := mload(add(data, 0x20)) } with no returndata length validation
a custom oracle returning <32 bytes or attacker-influenced data yields an arbitrary price
attacker_class: privileged (oracle impl is admin-set) — escalates only if impl is attacker-controlled or buggy
impact_estimate: Raw mload of staticcall returndata without length check; a malformed custom oracle can inject an arbitrary USD price into peg/minting. Bounded by admin trust in the oracle impl set, so Medium absent a permissionless way to register an impl.
evidence: LibUsdOracle.sol:167-174 low-level staticcall + unchecked assembly mload.

entry_conditions: Post-ReseedSilo: compare SUM(account stalk) to s.sys.silo.stalk.
violation_path: reseedSiloDeposit sets per-account stalk but never accumulates into a global s.sys.silo.stalk
init() does not set total stalk to the sum of issued stalk
global total stalk remains 0 or stale while accounts have stalk
impact_estimate: If global total stalk is not initialized to the sum of reseeded account stalk, earned-Bean distribution (which divides by total stalk) and governance quorum are mis-scaled. Needs confirmation of where total stalk is set in the broader reseed sequence (ReseedSun/InitalizeDiamond) — flagged Medium pending that.
evidence: ReseedSilo.sol writes only s.accts[].stalk and s.sys.silo.balances[].deposited/Bdv; no write to a system-wide total stalk in this file.

entry_conditions: User calls PipelineConvertFacet.pipelineConvert with crafted advancedPipe calls that re-enter the diamond while the deposit is removed and the new deposit BDV not yet booked.
violation_path: pipelineConvert removes source deposit
LibPipelineConvert executes user-supplied Pipeline calls (untrusted external)
if a re-entrant call reads/mutates silo balances mid-convert, BDV/stalk could be double counted
new deposit added with recomputed BDV
impact_estimate: Potential convert-time reentrancy / BDV inflation, but requires reading LibPipelineConvert.sol + ConvertFacet nonReentrant scoping and the well-reserve snapshot logic to confirm whether the manipulated reserves are used for BDV. Cannot fully trace from files read; flag for specialist (economic_attack/reentrancy).
evidence: PipelineConvertFacet.sol + LibPipelineConvert.sol invoke arbitrary Pipeline calls mid-convert; full reserve-snapshot and guard trace not completed in deep pass.

entry_conditions: An operator submits a signed Requisition (blueprint) to TractorFacet.tractor.
violation_path: LibTractor exposes _getBlueprintNonce / _incrementBlueprintNonce / maxNonce
the actual nonce<maxNonce enforcement lives in TractorFacet.tractor (not in scope files read)
if check is missing/off-by-one, blueprint replayed beyond maxNonce
attacker_class: operator (semi-privileged, blueprint must be signed by publisher)
impact_estimate: Blueprint replay would let an operator execute a publisher's order more than maxNonce times. Cannot confirm without TractorFacet.tractor body; LibTractor provides the primitives but not the enforcement. NEEDS_MORE_CONTEXT.
evidence: LibTractor.sol provides nonce primitives; enforcement and verifyRequisition are in beanstalk/farm/TractorFacet.sol which was not fully traced.

entry_conditions: A tractor blueprint execution reverts midway, or a nested tractor call occurs.
violation_path: _setPublisher requires activePublisher<=1 then sets publisher
if _resetPublisher is not guaranteed on the revert/return path, activePublisher stays set
_user() then returns the stale publisher for a subsequent unrelated call
impact_estimate: Stuck activePublisher could let actions execute on a stale publisher's behalf. _setPublisher guards against re-entry (require<=1), but the reset guarantee must be verified in TractorFacet. NEEDS_MORE_CONTEXT.
evidence: LibTractor.sol:93-104 _setPublisher/_resetPublisher; finally-path not visible without TractorFacet.tractor.

entry_conditions: Same as T-003; merkle leaf = keccak256(account, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots) — does NOT include reciever.
violation_path: leaf commits to owner+deposits only (line 127)
reciever is bound only by the owner's EIP-712 signature (lines 143-149)
anyone holding the signature can call with the chosen reciever
combined with no-replay (ACC-003) the deposits can be steered/duplicated
impact_estimate: reciever is not committed in the merkle leaf, so the migration credit is only as safe as signature secrecy + the (missing) replay guard. Reinforces T-003 as a duplicable, redirectable credit. High.
evidence: L2ContractMigrationFacet.sol:127 leaf excludes reciever; 143-149 signature is the only reciever binding.

entry_conditions: ReseedInternalBalances.init called with farmers[] and balances[] of unequal length.
violation_path: setInternalBalances loops i over farmers.length
reads internalBalances.balances[i] — if balances shorter, OOB revert; if longer, trailing balances ignored but total guard catches mismatch
no explicit farmers.length==balances.length require
attacker_class: no attacker — input-validation gap in one-shot init
impact_estimate: Mismatched arrays revert (DoS of internal-balance reseed) rather than silently corrupt, because totalInternalBalance guard (line 58) would also fail. Bounded; Medium (migration DoS if mis-supplied).
evidence: ReseedInternalBalances.sol:44-63: indexes balances[i] by farmers index, only a sum guard, no length-equality require.

entry_conditions: ReseedBarn.init given fertilizerIds NOT in ascending order (contract comment requires ascending but code does not enforce).
violation_path: mintFertilizers builds nextFid linked list assuming ascending order
i==0 sets fertFirst; nextFid[prev]=cur; last sets fertLast
out-of-order input produces a malformed/cyclic linked list
attacker_class: no attacker — input dependent on upgrade caller
impact_estimate: Malformed fertilizer linked list corrupts Sun fertilizer payout iteration (Beans paid to fertilizer in order). Could strand or mispay fertilizer. Bounded by trusted upgrade caller supplying correct order; Medium.
evidence: ReseedBarn.sol:76-95 builds nextFid chain with only the NatSpec 'MUST be ascending' as protection, no on-chain ordering check.
